message.abstract: <jats:p> Consider a convex set [Formula: see text], where G(x) is a symmetric matrix whose every entry is a polynomial or rational function, 𝒟 ⫅ ℝ<jats:sup>n</jats:sup> is a domain on which G(x) is defined, and [Formula: see text] means G(x) is positive semidefinite. The set S is called semidefinite representable if it equals the projection of a higher dimensional set that is defined by a linear matrix inequality (LMI). This paper studies sufficient conditions guaranteeing semidefinite representability of S. We prove that S is semidefinite representable in the following cases: (i) 𝒟 = ℝ<jats:sup>n</jats:sup>, G(x) is a matrix polynomial and matrix sos-concave; (ii) 𝒟 is compact convex, G(x) is a matrix polynomial and strictly matrix concave on 𝒟 (iii) G(x) is a matrix rational function and q-module matrix concave on 𝒟. Explicit constructions of semidefinite representations are given. Some examples are illustrated. </jats:p>
title: Polynomial Matrix Inequality and Semidefinite Representation
